reason: On this branch the logic is equivalent (same (s_ptr),Y reads in the same order for every row it finishes, C set at .dirty exactly when the old code would set it, A/Y dead after, X untouched; rn=0 gives the same 256-byte walk), and hazel_b here has room (&DF65 -> &DF6D). But the change is +8 bytes in hazel_b, and hazel_b is full on the gameplay branches that take main's changes: gameplay-shield (which contains main) and hud-rupture put level_movers_x_low, ground_columns and rup_k_lo/hi after sky_col_check under HUD_RUPTURE, so build/strykers-gameplay.lst has hazel_b_end = &DFFF, one byte short of the ASSERT hazel_b_end <= &E000. With 8 more bytes the gameplay disc (the published WIP, HUD_RUPTURE on) fails to assemble with 'HAZEL overruns by 7'. The gate's BUILDS on this branch do not include HUD_RUPTURE, so it would not see this. The candidate's relies_on ('nothing after it moves... below &E000') holds only for this branch's builds. A smaller cost: it also gives up the early exit on a dirty row (the whole row is read before BNE dirty) and makes a 1-byte row 3 cycles slower. Recount: old 15n-1 cycles a row of n clean bytes, new 13n+2 (n>1) or 17 (n=1). That saves 2n-3, about 9.2 a row at the measured ~6.1 bytes a row and 2.3 rows a pass (~21 a pass).
